review_note: review_required: a Potawatomi person of the gathering at Chicago in August 1812, the eve of the battle in which the garrison and its families were attacked. The card states only what the named sources say, says where a story is Kinzie family tradition rather than a contemporary account, and stages no speech or ceremony.

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: Wau-Bun puts his wigwam beside the stream 'along the present State Street', the creek the camp records follow; which lodge is not said.

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3461 sweep found in this household on 14 August is on the card.

persons.name: Wau-bee-nee-mah

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the afternoon of 14 August 1812, read from the evidence below; no source takes a roll call that afternoon.

persons.note: Chief, with a wigwam in the camp by the creek. Potawatomi, Illinois River. His family's wigwam stood in the encampment on the 15th, beside the creek (Wau-Bun, Mrs Helm); a lodge standing on the 15th was very likely pitched by the 14th. 15 and 16 August: Stretched a mat across two poles to screen Mrs Helm from the killing of a wounded prisoner. Afterwards: Unknown.

persons.name: The wife of Wau-bee-nee-mah

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the afternoon of 14 August 1812, read from the evidence below; no source takes a roll call that afternoon.

persons.note: Wau-Bun gives her no name of her own. Woman of the camp; gave Mrs Helm maple-sugar water. Potawatomi, Illinois River. At her wigwam by the creek on the 15th. 15 and 16 August: Dipped water from the stream, stirred in maple sugar with her hand and gave it to Mrs Helm. Afterwards: Unknown.
